filename: Control-Augmented Autoregressive Diffusion for Data Assimilation.pdf
title: Control-Augmented Autoregressive Diffusion for Data Assimilation
testbed_rationale: Focuses on data assimilation and autoregressive diffusion model control rather than subgrid parameterization; benchmark datasets are standard synthetic PDEs and derived ERA5 slices without specified data URLs/repositories.
pain_points: Long-horizon autoregressive drift and compounding errors in chaotic systems under sparse observations.
High computational cost of inference-time guidance, test-time optimization, and joint score evaluations in diffusion models.
Classical data assimilation methods (EnKF, 3D-Var, 4D-Var) degrade sharply under aggressive downsampling, non-Gaussianity, and highly sparse/delayed observations.
extraction_notes: The preprint is from arXiv (arXiv:2510.06637v3, dated May 2026). Stephan Mandt acknowledges support from the NSF LEAP Center. Code or repository links were not explicitly provided in the text (only a third-party reference implementation link to lucidrains/denoising-diffusion-pytorch is cited in Appendix G).
